blocks.content: Both the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts of 1992 created a constitutional mandate for democratic decentralization at the grass-roots level in India.

rows: 3-Tier: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zilla Parishad
3-Type: Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council, Municipal Corporation

items: Remember the subject count difference: 11th Schedule has 29 functional items for Panchayats, while 12th Schedule has 18 functional items for Municipalities.
Elections to local bodies are conducted by the State Election Commission (Article 243K/243ZA), NOT the Election Commission of India.
If a local body is dissolved prematurely, fresh elections must be held within 6 months, and the new body continues only for the remainder of the period.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Panchayats govern rural local self-government under Part IX (Articles 243 to 243O), whereas Municipalities govern urban local self-government under Part IXA (Articles 243P to 243ZG).
The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act added the 11th Schedule containing 29 functional subjects for Panchayats.
The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act added the 12th Schedule containing 18 functional subjects for Municipalities.
Both local bodies have a fixed tenure of 5 years and mandate a minimum of 33% seat reservation for women.
Elections to both bodies are conducted by the State Election Commission, and finances are reviewed by the State Finance Commission.
